prefLabel.value: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment
Security testing in development and acceptance

definition.value: Detective controls are designed to search for and identify errors or undesirable events after they have occurred so that corrective actions can be taken.

prefLabel.value: Installation of software on operational systems

definition.value: Directive controls give direction. These can be, for example, statutory obligations, regulatory standards including professional standards, or other organisational requirements or instructions, many of which are converted into policies, procedures, circulars, standard operating procedures and training.
Reactive controlsfocus on what happens after the risk occurs or which identify weaknesses in our current controls

prefLabel.value: Compliance with policies, rules and standards for information security

definition.value: objective and independent assurance, e.g. internal audit, providing reasonable (not absolute) assurance of the overall effectiveness of governance, risk management and controls.
Initial risk is the level of risk after existing controls are considered when the risk was originally assessed.
Proactive controls are put in place before the risk materialises
in order to monitor the action one person must have lead responsibility.

the way risks are managed and controlled day-to-day. Assurance comes directly from those responsible for delivering specific objectives or processes. Its value comes from those who know the business, culture and day-to-day challenges.

Any measure or action that modifies or regulates risk. Controls include any policy, procedure, practice, process, technology, technique, method, or device that modifies or regulates risk. They can exist or be required as additional in order to further mitigate the risk. Risk treatments become controls, or modify existing controls, once they are implemented. A mechanism, process, procedure or action which can be verified, that seeks to reduce the likelihood and/or consequence of a risk.

Personal protective equipment (PPE) includes clothing and devices to protect workers. PPE needs constant effort and attention (including proper use and training) from workers. Higher-level controls aren’t always feasible, and PPE might be needed in conjunction with other control measures. Least effective contols.
Inherent risk in the HSE is the level of risk before consideration of control and/or action measures.

Administrative controls change the way work is done or give workers more information by providing workers with relevant procedures, training, or warnings. They’re often used together with higher-level controls.
Corrective controls are designed to correct errors or undesirable events which have occurred and will prevent further occurrences.

prefLabel.value: Information security incident management planning and preparation
Information security awareness, education and training
Addressing information security within supplier agreements

definition.value: Avoid/Terminate it completely e.g. do not proceed with the planned activity.
Engineering controls reduce exposure by preventing hazards from coming into contact with workers. They still allow workers to do their jobs, though.

prefLabel.value: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets
Secure disposal or re-use of equipment
Information security for use of cloud services
Managing information security in the ICT supply chain

definition.value: Reduce the risk with further actions.

prefLabel.value: Separation of development, test and production environments

definition.value: Actions are a future measure that will maintain and/or modify a risk. In the HSE, an action is a future measure to further reduce either the likelihood or impact of a risk.

An ISO control is defined as a measure that modifies or maintains risk. Some of the controls in this document are controls that modify risk, while others maintain risk. An information security policy, for example, can only maintain risk, whereas compliance with the information security policy can modify risk.  Moreover, some controls describe the same generic measure in different risk contexts. This document provides a generic mixture of organizational, people, physical and technological information security controls derived from internationally recognized best practices.

prefLabel.value: Protection of information systems during audit testing

definition.value: Target risk in the HSE is the planned level of risk after consideration of both control and action measures.

prefLabel.value: Assessment and decision on information security events

definition.value: Preventative controls are controls designed to stop, discourage, pre-empt or limit the possibility of an undesirable event before it occurs.
Current risk is the level of risk after both the existing controls and actions are considered at the point in time the risk is being assessed

prefLabel.value: Inventory of information and other associated assets

definition.value: Elimination makes sure the hazard no longer exists. Most effective method
Risk treatment is the process to modify risk.
Accept the level of risk based on existing information e.g. pursue the opportunity.
Controls are measures that maintain and/or modify risk. In the HSE, a control is a measure that is in place, is working effectively and operating to reduce either the likelihood or impact of a risk.
Substitution means changing out a material or process to reduce the hazard.

prefLabel.value: Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services

definition.value: assurance from external independent assurance providers such as Regulators.
Residual risk in the HSE is the level of risk remaining after consideration of existing controls.

the way the organisation oversees the control framework so that it operates effectively. The assurance provided is separate from those responsible for delivery, but not independent of the management chain, such as risk and compliance functions.

prefLabel.value: Protecting against physical and environmental threats
Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements

definition.value: Transfer the risk e.g. to an identified individual or unit, that has been communicated to and notified, where many of the actions identified as required to mitigate are better managed and are within their span of control.
treatment plans detail both action and effective control plans, to minimise the likelihood and impact of the identified risk.
